title: Trading with the help of AI
author: MoneyFriendship5039
selftext:
I have been into trading for the last few years recently, and commited to it last year every day of the summer and learned a pretty cool concept called SMC. Recently, I switched from trading to startups and AI, and was wondering if anyone makes it so you can trade any strategy you want with AI where it crafts it from scratch with you, and backtests and paper trades like an actual person.

I have never seen anyone do that, was wondering if there is people out there. I know few like [public.com/agents](http://public.com/agents) and [composer.trade](http://composer.trade/), but those are all like 'if this happens do this', which is not what trading is. would love how you guys are trading with AI or managing your portfolios right now. :)

comments.author: Forexcalibur
comments.body: I have the opposite of “can trade any strategy you want with AI where it crafts it from scratch with you”.  I have a system where regardless of the strategy, AI tells you that it’s complete crap and it will never work.

replies.body: My ai tells me to build something and then after three hours of following its instructions it will tell me it has no idea whats its doing or that the whole thing is shit and delete it. Happened to me today. Twice.

replies.author: No-Consequence-1779
replies.body: I like that.  I think I can duplicate that system.

comments.author: Warm_Frame_3913
comments.body:
Genuine question on “if this happens do this”

What else would the AI write for you? Any strategy it crafts from your inputs will end up being a “if this happens do this” ruleset in order to prove a historical edge, improve future decision making, or shape a plausible edge

Without the ruleset the alternative is having the model reason over each trade live like a person, ill argue theres nothing local strong enough to do this sort of task on its own, leaving you paying for compute. It’s much more expensive and much harder to prove a historical edge.

If it answers different on every call, you cant reproduce anything. And if it drifts, goodluck there. 

Ill argue real trading is based on rules, I’ll point you at algorithms, quant firms, HFT, and any other rule based trading system. (There everywhere now)

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: The thing Composer and the public agents can't do is write and change the actual strategy logic. They're deterministic block builders, so you're still the one deciding the rules and they just execute them. What you're describing is closer to a research assistant that writes the strategy, backtests it, actually reads the equity curve and drawdown, and then rewrites itself to fix what broke. That's a different category from the if this then that stuff. It does exist now, it's just early. I'm building one (AutoQuant) where you describe an idea in plain English, the AI generates the strategy code, backtests it on real data, and loops on the results to improve it, then you paper trade it through your own Alpaca account. Not the only project heading this direction, but the code generating and iterating part is the piece the rule builders skip. Happy to get into specifics, and fair warning I'm biased since I make it.

comments.author: Sufficient_Dig207
comments.body:
Trading on Kalshi with my ai agents right now. Still paying the tuition. I have tried to have the AI agents do the research, implement, and backtest. Didn't work. The original idea, and winning strategy has to come from human.

It amplifies what you have, either the win or the loss.
